To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sophisticated software profiling techniques that are used to generate path profiles are not suitable for hot path prediction in an online setting and that less is more when it comes to software profiling for hot path detection.

1) sophisticated profiling schemes that are accurate offline are ill-suited to be used in online settings, and 2) low-overhead profiling schemes that exhibit low runtime overhead are more effective than sophisticated profiling schemes in online settings.
sophisticated path profile based hot path prediction schemes, if used online, are too slow and too expensive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to best use the available profile data for hot path prediction in a dynamic code generation setting.
the question of whether sophisticated profiling techniques are necessary for hot path prediction in dynamic code generation systems or if simpler schemes are sufficient.
the question: How to achieve high quality hot path prediction with minimal profiling overhead?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the less profiling you do the more effective your predictions will be.
sophisticated software profiling techniques are not well suited for dynamic code generation systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the key to effective hot path prediction in a dynamic code generation system is to make early predictions that are accurate enough for the task at hand.
sophisticated path profile based software profiling schemes are ill-suited to dynamic systems and that less profiling is actually better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in order to make effective use of profile information in dynamic code generation systems, the profiling schemes should be designed with runtime constraints in mind.
in order to achieve good prediction quality, the profiling scheme must be simple and exhibit low runtime overhead.
sophisticated profiling schemes are not always beneficial.
